## Design

### 2026-10-24 – In this session, I finished the schematic, added the footprints (except for the keypads), and imported it into the PCB editor. This is how my schematic looks right now:

**3h**

In this session, I finished the schematic, added the footprints (except for the keypads), and imported it into the PCB editor. This is how my schematic looks right now:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 6.06.17 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/0f0e9d4b661fbcd712359223607b032ea4f2dceb425705696deaac773f808f96.png)

Instead of going with the guide, I decided to do something a little different. I decided to add a second encoder, and use both of the encoder's switches. Since I didn't have enough room on the ESP32, I got rid of the low-profile switches and a slider. The remaining slider will be used to control the volume. For the first encoder, it will control the octaves, and the second octave will be a modulation wheel. The switches will reset the octave/mod effect. These are my footprints:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 6.13.05 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/373f67d4db0adfe4cea371057a22df7983b029184e4e8ab1961257d43184c35b.png)

And finally this is how it looks like in the PCB editor (without the keys):

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 6.14.59 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/61388d0a4828528001e6c922482e0810183ffd3bf73c4e10d16d5baba333a6f7.png)

I spent a lot of the time on the schematic and thinking on what parts I should sacrifice for the second encoder.

### 2026-10-25 – I finished the PCB. Next session I will do all of the firmware and software stuff. Here is how the final PCB looks:

**6h**

I finished the PCB. Next session I will do all of the firmware and software stuff. Here is how the final PCB looks:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 9.40.49 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/5f92e613214f33b12a6de0c3e809d0c1b068bf99265b7d95074ad5a28f2fb18d.png)

It is similar to the guide, however I changed it by adding a second encoder. Since I did that and also am using their switch functionalities, I had to remove the 3 low-profile switches and one slider to make room on the ESP32.

Now, onto what I did. In the previous session I finished the schematic, so the first thing I did this session was create the footprint for the keys. This is what I ended up with (similar to the guide's, since I lke the piano keys style they used):

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 7.19.43 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/3bb855e7c06d41bd7e1e191bd9203caf91b6efb91b11b3c4e1586acc9b8958fa.png)

After moving everything around, this is the layout I settled with:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 7.47.14 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/a6d07fe3686d97a348144477a7ed779bdd8aa34b176cf5b174092cb5a8c8dfcc.png)

Wiring everything up took the longest time, especially with the LEDs. After spending a long time attempting to wire it up, I think it might have been impossible. However, I got through this by flipping D1 and D3 upside down. It still took a while but this is the final result of the wiring:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 10.29.25 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/05ca2ebb7da7e4258c7c198b25f0629f651bb1449a57af92329390e41f5df00a.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 10.29.37 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/651709e5900174571de004a6e15dbd10152045b6bd140c2fdb90e4dc71df6cf1.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 10.29.46 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/33cdc3b4fa62a899d142ca5b12681cfcac8124165d76dde457656151eca97c2e.png)

Finally, I added a design to the front silkscreen (you can see it from the previous images). I decided to go with something simple, since there wasn't much room on the front:

![Screenshot 2026-10-24 at 9.22.41 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/7ME5CuFiz5X4u2KxuO278yO001rQ8Db2/9061c560f0abed508d2eb10acbacfbcc4567eb9713750d57369f05a1793f09a0.png)

After that, I ended the session with downloading the gerber files.
